title: Green laser guys:  Do you find red stuff to disappear?

posts.topic_title: Green laser guys:  Do you find red stuff to disappear?
posts.author: Justin W
posts.post_subject: Green laser guys:  Do you find red stuff to disappear?
posts.content_md:
Howdy all

I lase at 532nm and feel like I've noticed before that anything colored red seems to become oddly colorless under green laser illumination.

I am designing a new plateholder and am considering coloring it red instead of black in an effort to have it not appear in holograms.

Has anyone else who lases green tried this?

posts.topic_title: Green laser guys:  Do you find red stuff to disappear?
posts.author: Kiffdino
posts.post_subject: Green laser guys:  Do you find red stuff to disappear?
posts.content_md:
i dont see the point colouring your holder red.

black will always suck up more light then red...

of yourse your lab will look nicer in daylight

posts.topic_title: Green laser guys:  Do you find red stuff to disappear?
posts.author: MichaelH
posts.post_subject: Green laser guys:  Do you find red stuff to disappear?
posts.content_md:
And depending on the quality and specific mix of the paint you may actually find that red glows a bit under green light and ends up looking more like yellow.

Go with flat black.

10-4 and roger, good buddies!

Flat black it is.

Thanks for getting back to me on this one.

posts.topic_title: Green laser guys:  Do you find red stuff to disappear?
posts.author: Hans
posts.post_subject: Green laser guys:  Do you find red stuff to disappear?
posts.content_md: I discovered by accident that blood is totally invisible in red safe light and black in green laser light. I cut my hand on a glass plate and did not see any blood in the safe light, so figured it was just a scratch. Then when I went to adjust the laser beam and saw black spots on my hands. I turned on the white light and my garage looked like a scene from Friday 13th. Amazing...all the places ones hand touches in the timespan of about 10 minutes.
